title: Private upgrade cadence controller and state translation utility for orchestrated migrations
creator: Sofia Liang
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) need a safe, observable way to roll out platform upgrades that include binary changes, state migrations, and schema changes. Current tooling lacks a deterministic cadence controller and an automated state translation helper for agent/DB state so upgrades either require manual coordination or brittle ad-hoc scripts.
goal: Deliver an upgrade cadence controller and a companion state-translation utility that together enable automated, safe, resumable orchestrated migrations across Private clusters with canary/percentage rollouts, preflight checks, and transparent telemetry for SLOs and rollback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Cadence controller can schedule phased rollouts by percentage or fixed groups and supports pause/resume/cancel operations via the Console API

State translation utility supports dry-run mode and produces deterministic transformation plans for agent runtime state and two major DB schema change patterns (additive denormalized field + column split/merge)
Preflight checks run automatically and can block rollouts when >3% of nodes fail health/compatibility checks
Automatic rollback trigger exists and is exercised in an end-to-end test (failed canary triggers revert path with documented metrics)
Telemetry emitted for per-stage success/failure, latency regression, tokenization cost delta, and migration duration; renders in Console runtime dashboard
Security review signed off for the state-translation binary and agent handshake protocol (KMS keys not exfiltrated, ephemeral credentials used)
implementation_notes: Controller: CRON-like cadence + event-driven state machine. Store stage metadata in versioned rollout objects in the Private control plane DB. Each stage maps to a target set (percent, label selector, or explicit node IDs).
State translation: implement as library + CLI that can be run in agent sandbox. Translation plans are generated from a compatibility matrix and are idempotent via applied checksums.
Migration pattern support: start with two patterns: (1) additive field with backfill job; (2) column split requiring write-forwarding (writer writes both old and new columns for a window).
Rollback: cheap rollback policy prefers binary downgrade where schema is forward-compatible; otherwise route traffic away and run reverse-translation job where safe.
Gates: health, perf (p50/p95 latency thresholds), error-rate, and custom user QA tag. Gate evaluation frequency default 2 minutes, configurable per rollout.
API: add /rollouts endpoint to Console API with actions: start, pause, resume, cancel, status, explain-plan, dry-run. Ensure RBAC rules map to existing Private roles.
Compatibility: incorporate model/runtime compatibility matrix to decide whether a node can be upgraded in-place or needs to be replaced (e.g., quantization format mismatch).
Testing: create a simulation harness that runs the controller against recorded cluster topologies to validate scheduling heuristics and failure modes.

notes_on_tradeoffs: We prioritize resumability and observable state over a fully-automated zero-touch migration. This increases initial complexity but reduces blast radius during early rollouts.
Percentage-based rollouts are intuitive but brittle under node churn; we will support affinity-based groups (by rack/region) as the more stable default for large clusters.
Full automated DB migrations (semantic transforms) are out of scope for MVP; instead we produce deterministic, reviewable plans and a backfill job that operators can inspect before apply.
